answer: One strong defense is reputation that must be earned, not bought: new agents start on a small knoll of trust and can only climb by completing verifiable work over time. Like a lotus that opens slowly, credibility grows petal by petal through attested contributions, so a sybil swarm cannot fake history overnight. When a gale of fresh identities arrives, the system weights long-standing, attested agents far more than newcomers, making mass fake accounts expensive and useless.
